questions.problem: What is the center of the hyperbola $\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{5}-\frac{(y-4)^{2}}{6}=1?$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Note that the given equation can be rewritten as follows:

$$
\frac{(x-(-2))^{2}}{(\sqrt{5})^{2}}-\frac{(y-4)^{2}}{(\sqrt{6})^{2}}=1
$$

In this case, $h=-2$ and $k=4.$

Therefore, the center of the hyperbola is $(-2,4).$

questions.problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$6{x}^{2}-5{y}^{2}+72x+70y=59?$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}^{2}-5{y}^{2}+72x+70y & =59 \\ 6{x}^{2}+72x-5{y}^{2}+70y & =59 \\ 6[{x}^{2}+12x]-5[{y}^{2}-14y] & =59 \\ 6((x+6)^{2}-36)-5[(y-7)^{2}-49] & =59 \\ 6(x+6)^{2}-216-5(y-7)^{2}+245 & =59 \\ 6(x+6)^{2}-5(y-7)^{2} & =59+216-245 \\ 6(x+6)^{2}-5(y-7)^{2} & =30 \\ \frac{(x+6)^{2}}{5}-\frac{(y-7)^{2}}{6} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center is $(-6,7).$

canonical_examples.problem:

$4 y^2  - 10 x^2 - 8 y  - 40 x  = 76?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\dfrac{(y-k)^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{(x-h)^2}{b^2}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}-10{x}^{2}-8y-40x & =76 \\ 4{y}^{2}-8y-10{x}^{2}-40x & =76 \\ 4[{y}^{2}-2y]-10[{x}^{2}+4x] & =76 \\ 4[(y-1)^{2}-1]-10[(x+2)^{2}-4] & =76 \\ 4(y-1)^{2}-4-10(x+2)^{2}+40 & =76 \\ 4(y-1)^{2}-10(x+2)^{2} & =76-40+4 \\ 4(y-1)^{2}-10(x+2)^{2} & =40 \\ \frac{(y-1)^{2}}{10}-\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{4} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the center is $(-2,1)$.
